subject: Mutual action plan: MedixApp POC environment & network setup

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medixapp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan: MedixApp POC environment & network setup

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Following up with a concise mutual action plan (MAP) draft for the POC environment we discussed. Goal: get a production-like eval environment standing by Aug 23 so your data scientists can begin throughput/latency tests the week of Aug 24.

High-level asks (owner / target) —
- Redwood: provide tenant org and test API keys (Grace) — target by Aug 13
- Customer: confirm AWS account ID, VPC ID, and IP allowlist entries (Claire/IT) — target by Aug 13
- Redwood infra: prepare VPC peering instructions + route table change set (Jonas) — target by Aug 16
- Joint: smoke test + sample prompts (both) — target Aug 20–22

Technical specifics we need from you to proceed:
1) Customer AWS account ID for peering and cross-account role (if you prefer automated peering)
2) VPC ID (cidr: prefer /16 or /20) and a small set of test subnets to allow for egress rules
3) IP ranges to add to our API allowlist (your NAT/egress IPs) or confirmation that you'll accept peered traffic

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (action tracker), network-diagram.pdf (proposed peering topology).

If timeline looks tight on your side, tell us which items you'd prefer to shift — we can stage access (API keys first, peering second) to unblock testing earlier.

Next step: can you confirm the AWS account ID and the primary networking contact so we can loop them directly into the peering task?

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Grace —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. We're aligned on the objectives and Aug 23 is reasonable, though our network team asked a couple quick clarifying questions before they start the peering work:

- Do you require a cross-account IAM role for automated peering, or will a manual console peering request suffice?
- For the API allowlist: do you need our public egress IPs, or is peering enough for API auth?
- We will also need the SOC2 / data handling summary to include in the ticket to our security team; can you share the specific artifact?

I'll loop in our network engineer (cc'd) — they will be the primary for provide VPC details. We'll try to gather the above by EOD Aug 13.

Thanks,
Claire Wong
VP Data Science | MedixApp

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: MedixApp POC environment & network setup (technical follow-up)

Grace / Karthik —

Quick technical note to support Claire's questions:

1) We can support both options: automated cross-account role (preferred for faster lifecycle) or manual peering. If MedixApp wants automated peering, we'll need an IAM role ARN with a trust policy for redwood-peering@redwood-accounts.

2) For the API allowlist, peering alone will not enable public API endpoint calls unless they route via NAT. Our recommended pattern is
   - Option A: Add your public egress IPs to our API allowlist (fastest for smoke tests)
   - Option B: Set up VPC peering and route table entries to allow peered traffic; we'll also provision a private endpoint if you prefer private-only access (this takes longer).

3) Required info from customer to prepare our template: AWS account ID, VPC ID, preferred CIDR blocks for the peering connection, and a contact for BGP / route table changes (if applicable).

Attaching peering-template.txt that includes exact steps we send to customers. I'll prepare the Redwood-side route change bundle once Claire shares the VPC ID. Targeting to have that bundle by Aug 16.

- Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Claire / team —

Perfect, thanks for the VPC info and NAT IPs — that is everything we need to start. Short answers to your questions:
- Test API keys: issued per-tenant, revocable immediately from the console. Default TTL is 30 days for eval keys; we can shorten to 7 or 14 days if you'd like (let us know).
- NACLs: generally no changes required beyond route table entries for the peered CIDRs unless you have restrictive NACL rules; our peering-template includes a quick NACL checklist.
- SOC2: attaching a redacted SOC2 summary and our data handling FAQ in the MAP-final.xlsx.

Revised MAP and deliverables:
- Aug 13: Redwood issues org + temporary keys (Grace) — DONE / in flight
- Aug 16: Redwood provides route-change bundle + peering request template (Jonas)
- Aug 18: Customer submits peering and route updates (MedixApp IT)
- Aug 20–22: Joint smoke test window
- Aug 23: POC acceptance sign-off and next steps / pricing discussion

Links: HubSpot deal MDX-4821: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/MDX-4821
DocuSign (for SOW once POC accepted): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/status?envelopeId=abc123docusign

I'll attach MAP-final.xlsx (updated action tracker) to this thread and share the SOC2 summary inside it. If you prefer, we can also do a 20-minute handoff with your network engineer tomorrow morning to walk the peering steps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you running.
